title: Dandy Dick
text: INTRODUCTORY NOTE.

title: Dandy Dick
text: "Dandy Dick" was the third of the farces which Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Pinero wrote for the old Court Theatre--a series of plays which, besides giving playgoers a fresh source of laughter, and the English stage a new order of comic play, brought plentiful prosperity to the joint management of Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Arthur Cecil and the late Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: John Clayton.

title: Dandy Dick
text: But a kind of melancholy interest attaches to "Dandy Dick," for this play was, as it were, the swan-song of the old theatre and of the Clayton and Cecil partnership; and it was the piece in which Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Clayton was acting when death overtook him, to the general grief.

title: Dandy Dick
text: The production of "Dandy Dick" may be considered as something of a _tour de force_ in its way.

title: Dandy Dick
text: "The Schoolmistress" was at the end of its successful run, and Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Pinero was under contract to supply its successor by a certain date, when Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Clayton one day went down to Brighton, where the dramatist was then at work, to hear him read the two completed acts of the new play.

title: Dandy Dick
text: To Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Clayton's consternation, however, Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Pinero announced that he was dissatisfied with his work, and proposed to begin an entirely new play, as he had a more promising idea.

title: Dandy Dick
text: But time was pressing, and a successor to "The Schoolmistress" was an immediate necessity.

title: Dandy Dick
text: However, Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Pinero's idea of writing a play round a dean, who, while being a paragon of dignity and decorum, should be driven by an indiscreet act into a most undignified dilemma, appealed to Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Clayton, and hastening back to London with the sketches for the requisite scenes, he left Mr.

title: Dandy Dick
text: Pinero to set to work at once upon the new scheme.

title: Dandy Dick
text: And within a few weeks, indeed by the time the scenery was ready, the new play was completed, the rural constable of a village adjacent to Brighton having suggested the character of Noah Topping.

title: Dandy Dick
text: "Dandy Dick" was produced at the Court Theatre on January 27th, 1887, and, meeting with a most favorable initial reception, it settled down immediately into a complete success.

title: Dandy Dick
text: THE FIRST ACT.

title: Dandy Dick
text: _The morning-room in the Deanery of St. Marvells, with a large arched opening leading to the library on the right, and a deeply-recessed window opening out to the garden on the left. It is a bright spring morning, and an air of comfort and serenity pervades the place._ _SALOME, a tall, handsome, dark girl, of about three-and-twenty, is sitting with her elbows resting on her knees, staring wildly into vacancy. SHEBA, a fair little girl of about seventeen, wearing short petticoats, shares her despondency, and lies prostrate upon the settee._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh! oh my! oh my! oh my!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Sitting upright._] Oh, my gracious goodness, goodness gracious me! [_They both walk about excitedly._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. There's only one terrible word for it--it's a fix!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. It's worse than that! It's a scrape! How did you ever get led into it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. How did _we_ get led into it? Halves, Sheba, please.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. It was Major Tarver's proposal, and I believe, Salome, that it is to _you_ Major Tarver is paying attention.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. The Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone is promoted by the Officers of the Hussars. I believe that the young gentleman you have impressed calls himself an officer, though he is merely a lieutenant.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Indignantly._] Mr. Darbey is _certainly_ an officer--a small officer. How dare you gird at me, Salome?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Very well, then. When to-night we appear at the Durnstone Athenaeum, unknown to dear Papa, on the arms of Major Tarver and Mr. Darbey, I consider that we shall be equally wicked. Oh, how can we be so wrong?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Well, we're not wrong yet. We're only _going_ to be wrong; that's a very different matter.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. That's true. Besides, there's this to remember--we're inexperienced girls and have only dear Papa. But oh, now that the Ball is to-night, I repent, Sheba, I repent!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. I sha'n't do that till to-morrow. But oh, how I _shall_ repent to-morrow!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Taking an envelope from her pocket, and almost crying._] You'd repent now if you had seen the account for the fancy dresses.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Has it come in?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes, the Major enclosed it to me this morning. You know, Sheba, Major Tarver promised to get the dresses made in London, so I gave him our brown paper patterns to send to the _costumier._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Shocked._] Oh, Salome, do you think he quizzed them?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. No; I sealed them up and marked outside "To be opened only by a lady."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. That's all right. I hate the plan of myself in brown paper.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Well, of course Major Tarver begged to be allowed to pay for the dresses, and I said I couldn't dream of permitting it, and then he said he should be most unhappy if he didn't, and, just as I thought he was going to have his own way, [_bursting into tears_] he cheered up and said he'd yield to a lady. [_Taking a large account from the envelope._] And oh! he's yielded.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Read it! Don't spare me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Reading._] "Debtor to Lewis Isaacs, _Costumier_ to the Queen, Bow Street. One gown--period French Revolution, 1798--Fifteen guineas!"

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Sinking on her knees, clutching the table._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. "Trimmings, linings, buttons, frillings--Seven guineas!"

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Hysterically._] Yah!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. That's mine!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Putting her fingers into her ears._] Now for mine, oooh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Reading._] "One skirt and bodice--flower girl--period uncertain--Ten guineas."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Less than yours! What a shame!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. "Trimmings, linings, buttons, frillings--Five guineas! Extras, Two guineas. Total, Forty pounds, nineteen. Ladies' own brown paper patterns mislaid. Terms, Cash!" [_They throw themselves into each other's arms._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh, Sheba!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Salome! Are there forty pounds in the wide world?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. My heart weighs twenty. What shall we do?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. If we were only a few years older I should suggest that we wrote nice notes to Papa and committed suicide.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Brought up as we have been, that's out of the question!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Then let us be brave women and wear the dresses!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Of course we'll do that, but--the bill!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We must get dear Papa in a good humor and coax him to make us a present of money. He knows we haven't been charitable in the town for ever so long.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Poor dear Papa! He hasn't paid our proper dressmaker's bill yet, and I'm sure he's pressed for money.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. But we can't help that when _we're_ pressed for money--poor dear Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Suppose poor Papa refuses to give us a present?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Then we must play the piano when he's at work on his Concordance--poor dear Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. However, don't let us wrong poor Papa in advance. Let us try to think how nice we shall look.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh yes--sha'n't I!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh, I shall! And as for stealing out of the house with Major Tarver when poor dear Papa has gone to bed, why, Gerald Tarver would die for me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. So would Nugent Darbey for me; besides I'm not old enough to know better.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. You're not so very much younger than I, Sheba!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Indeed, Salome! Then why do you keep me in short skirts?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Why! you cruel girl! You know I can't lengthen you till I'm married! [_BLORE, the butler, a venerable-looking person, with rather a clerical suggestion about his dress, enters by the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. [_Benignly._] The two soldier gentlemen have just rode hup, Miss Salome. [_The girls clutch each other's hands._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. You mean Major Tarver?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. And Mr. Darbey. They have called to inquire after poor Papa.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Poor Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Shall I show them hin, Miss Sheba?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes, Blore, dear, and hang your h's on the hat-stand. [BLORE _laughs sweetly at SHEBA and shakes his fingers at her playfully._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. [_Vindictively, behind their backs._] 'Ussies! [_He goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Am I all right, Sheba?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes. Am I?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes. [_Looking out at window._] Here they are! How well Gerald Tarver dismounts! Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. He left his liver in India, didn't he?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. No--only part of it.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Well--part of it.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. And that he gave to his Queen, brave fellow!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Seating herself in an artificial attitude._] Where shall we be--here?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Running to the piano._] All right; you be admiring my voice!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, I dare say!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Here they are, and we're doing nothing!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Let's run away and then come in unconsciously.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes--unconsciously. [_They run off through the Library. BLORE shows in MAJOR TARVER and MR. DARBEY, who are both in regimentals. MAJOR TARVER is a middle-aged, tall, angular officer, with a thin face, yellow complexion, and red eyes. He is alternately in a state of great excitement and depression. MR. DARBEY is a mere boy, but with a pompous, patronizing manner._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. The Dean's out of the way, eh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Yes, sir, he his.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Eh? How is the Dean? Never mind--perhaps Miss Jedd is at home?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Yes, sir, she his.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. It would be discourteous to run away without asking Miss Jedd after her father.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_Throwing himself on the settee._] Deuced bad form!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. The ladies were 'ere a minute ago. [_SALOME and SHEBA walk in together. SALOME has her arm round her sister's waist and looks up to her with a sweet, trusting smile. They start in confusion on seeing TARVER and DARBEY._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Major Tarver.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Mr. Darbey.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Taking SALOME'S hand eagerly._] My dear Miss Jedd!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_Rising and putting a glass to his eye._] Hah yah! Hah yah!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_With her hand on her heart._] You quite startled us.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_In an agony of contrition._] Oh, did we?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Awfully cut up to hear it.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We never dreamt of finding two visitors for Papa.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Why, you told me to show the gentlemen hin, Miss Sheba! [_The two girls start guiltily and glare at BLORE._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_With suppressed rage_.] You needn't wait, Blore!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. [_To himself._] Let 'em 'ang that on the 'atstand! [_BLORE goes out. DARBEY and SHEBA stroll together into the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To SALOME._] We thought we'd ride over directly after parade to make the final arrangements for tonight. Have the costumes arrived?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes, they came yesterday in a hamper labeled "Miss Jedd, Secretary, Cast-off Clothing Distribution League."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. That was my idea--came to me in the middle of the night.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Dear Major Tarver, surely this terrible strain on your nerves is very, very bad for you with your--your----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. My liver--say the word, Miss Jedd.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Drooping her head._] Oh, Major Tarver!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. It is frightfully injurious. Of course I'm excited now, and you see me at my best, but the alternating fits of hopeless despondency are shocking to witness and to endure!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. It's all that damned India! Oh! what have I said! You will never forgive me.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Indeed, indeed I will!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Never. Oh, Miss Jedd, my forgetfulness has brought me--one of my--terrible attacks--of depression!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Major Tarver! [_She leads him to a chair into which he sinks in a ghastly state. DARBEY strolls in from the Library with SHEBA._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To SHEBA._] Your remarks about the army are extremely complimentary. On behalf of the army I thank you. We fellows are not a bad sort, take us all round.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. There's a grand future before you, isn't there?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Well, I suppose there is if I go on as I'm going now.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To SALOME._] Thanks, the attack has passed. Now about to-night; at what time is the house entirely quiet?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Poor dear Papa goes round with Blore at half-past nine--after that all is rest and peacefulness.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Then if we're here with the closed carriage at ten--! [_They go together into the library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To SHEBA._] Some of us army men can slave too. Tarver's queer livah has thrown all the arrangements for the Fancy Ball on my shoulders. [_SALOME and TARVER re-enter._] Look at him--that's when he's enjoying life!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Laughing convulsively._] Ha! ha! ha! ho! he! he! Good, eh, Miss Jedd?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. But suppose dear Papa should hear us crunching down the gravel path!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Oh! [_He sinks on to the settee with a vacant stare, his arms hanging helplessly._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To SHEBA._] There--now his career is a burden to him!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Would you like a glass of water, Major Tarver?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Taking SALOME'S hand._] Thank you, dear Miss Jedd, with the least suggestion of cayenne pepper in it.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Looking out at window._] Oh, Salome! Papa! Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. The Dean?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. The Dean! [_They all collect themselves in a fluster. The two girls go to meet their father, who enters at the window with his head bowed and his hands behind his back, in deep thought. THE DEAN is a portly man of about fifty, with a dignified demeanor, a suave voice and persuasive manner, and a noble brow surmounted by silver-gray hair. BLORE follows THE DEAN, carrying some books, a small bunch of flowers, and an umbrella._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Tenderly._] Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Papsey! [_THE DEAN rouses himself, discovers his children and removes his hat._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_To SALOME._] Salome! [_To SHEBA._] My toy-child! [_He draws the girls to him and embraces them, then sees TARVER and DARBEY._] Dear me! Strangers! TARVER _and_ Darbey. [_Coughing uncomfortably._] H'm!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Reproachfully, taking his hat from him._] Papa! Major Tarver and Mr. Darbey have ridden over from Durnstone to ask how your cold is. [_SHEBA takes the gold-rimmed pince-nez which hangs upon THE DEAN'S waistcoat and places it before his eyes._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Dear me! Major! Mr. Garvey.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Mr. Darbey!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Darbey! How good of you! [_With his girls still embracing him he extends a hand to each of the men._] My cold is better. [_BLORE goes out through the Library._] Major--Mr. Garvey--these inquiries strike me as being so kind that I insist--no, no, I _beg_ that you will share our simple dinner with us to-night at six o'clock!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Disconcerted._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. H'm!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Let me see--Tuesday night is----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Leg of mutton, Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Thank you. Mutton, hot.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. And custards, Papsey.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Thank you, toy-child--custards, cold. And a welcome--warm.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Looking to SALOME._] Well, I--ah--[_SALOME nods her head to him violently._] That is, certainly, Dean, certainly.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Delighted, my dear Dean--delighted! [_THE DEAN gives DARBEY a severe look, and with an important cough walks into the Library. The men and the girls speak in undertones._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Depressed._] Now, what will happen to-night?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Why, don't you see, as you will have to drive over to dine, you will both be here, on the spot, ready to take us back to Durnstone? [_THE DEAN sits at his desk in the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Of course; when we're turned out we can hang about in the lane till you're ready.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Yes, but when are _we_ to make our preparations? It'll take me a long time to look like Charles the First!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We can drive about Durnstone while you dress.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_To TARVER, admiringly._] Charles the First! Oh, Major!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. That was my idea--Charles the Martyr, you know. Tarver's a martyr to his liver--see?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh! sha'n't we all look magnificent?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Grand idea--the whole thing!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Regular army notion! [_They are all in a state of great excitement when THE DEAN re-enters, with an anxious look, carrying a bundle of papers._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Here is Papa! [_They rush to various seats, all in constrained attitudes._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To THE DEAN._] We waited to say--good-morning.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Taking his hand, abstractedly._] How kind! Good-morning!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Six o'clock sharp, Dean?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. At six, punctually. Salome, represent me by escorting these gentlemen to the gate. [_SALOME, TARVER, and DARBEY go out. SHEBA is following slyly when THE DEAN looks up from his papers._] Sheba!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Papsey!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Check me in a growing tendency to dislike Mr. Garvey. At dinner, Sheba, watch that I carve for him fairly.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes, Papsey! [_THE DEAN turns away and sits on the settee. SHEBA, with her head down and her hands folded, walks towards the door, and then bounds out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Turning the papers over in his hand, solemnly._] Bills! [_He rises, walks thoughtfully to a chair, sits and examines papers again._] Bills! [_He rises again, walks to another chair, and sinks into it with a groan._] Bills! _SALOME and SHEBA re-enter._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_To SHEBA, in a whisper._] Papa's alone!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. A beautiful opportunity to ask for that little present of money. Poor dear Papa! SALOME _and_ Sheba. Poor dear Papa! [_They link their hands together and walk as if going out through the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Looking up._] Don't go, children! [_He rises, the girls rush to him, and laughing with joy they turn him like a top, dancing round him._ [_Panting._] Stop, children!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Papsey's in a good humor!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Pinching his chin._] He always is!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Papsey will listen to our little wants! [_They force him into a chair. SALOME sits on the ground embracing his legs, SHEBA lies on the top of the table._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Oh dear, oh dear! Your wants are very little ones. What are they, Salome? What are they, toy-child?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Papa! Have you any spare cash?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Spare cash! Playful Salome!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. _L--s--d,_ Papsey, or _L--s,_ Papsey, and never mind the--_d._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Ha! ha! I am glad, really glad, children, that you have broken through a reserve which has existed on this point for at least a fortnight--and babbled for money.

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. [_Laughing with delight._] Ha! ha!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. It gives me the opportunity of meeting your demands with candor. Children, I have love for you, solicitude for you, but--I have no spare cash for anybody. [_He rises and walks gloomily across to the piano, on the top of which he commences to arrange his bills. In horror SALOME scrambles up from the floor, and SHEBA wriggles off the table. Simultaneously they drop on to the same chair and huddle together._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_To herself._] Lost!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_To herself._] Done for!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. And now you have so cheerily opened the subject, let me tell you with equal good humor [_emphatically flourishing the bills_] that this sort of thing must be put a stop to. Your dressmaker's bill is shocking; your milliner gives an analytical record of the feverish beatings of the hot pulse of fashion; your general draper blows a rancorous blast which would bring dismay to the stoutest heart. Let me for once peal out a deep paternal bass to your childish treble and say emphatically--I've had enough of it! [_He paces up and down. The two girls utter a loud yell of grief._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Through her tears._] We've been brought up as young ladies--that can't be done for nothing!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Sheba's small, but she cuts into a lot of material.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My girls, it is such unbosomings as this which preserve the domestic unison of a family. Weep, howl, but listen. The total of these weeds which spring up in the beautiful garden of paternity is a hundred and fifty-six, eighteen, three. Now, all the money I can immediately command is considerably under five hundred pounds.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh, Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh! what a lot!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Hush! But read, Salome, read aloud this paragraph in "The Times" of yesterday. There, my child. [_He hands a copy of "The Times" to SALOME with his finger upon a paragraph._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Reading._] "A Munificent Offer. Dr. Jedd, the Dean of St. Marvells, whose anxiety for the preservation of the Minister Spire threatens to undermine his health, has subscribed the munificent sum of one thousand pounds to the Restoration Fund." [_Indignantly._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh! and we gasping for clothing!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Read on, my child.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Reading._] "On condition that seven other donors come forward, each with the like sum."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. And will they?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Anxiously._] My darling, times are bad, but one never knows.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. If they don't!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Then you will have your new summer dresses as usual.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Hoarsely._] But if they do! Speak, Father!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Gloomily._] Then we will all rejoice!

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. Rejoice!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. And retrench. Two R's, little ones. Retrench and Rejoice. [_The two girls cling to each other as BLORE comes from the Library with two letters on a salver._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. The second post, sir--just hin.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Blandly._] Thank you.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. [_Hearing SALOME and SHEBA crying._] They've 'ad a scolding, 'ussies. Let 'em 'ang that on the 'atstand! [_He is going out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Opening letters._] Oh, Blore! This note from Mr. Hodder, the Secretary of "The Sport and Relaxation Repression Guild," reminds me that to-morrow is the first day of the Races--the St. Marvells Spring Meeting, as it is called.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Hindeed, sir--fancy that! And I not know it!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. All our servants may not resemble you, Blore. Pray remind them in the kitchen and the stable of the rule of the house----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. No servant allowed to leave the Deanery, on hany pretence, while the Races is on.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Kindly._] While the races _are_ on--thank you, Blore. [_Opens his second letter._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Thank _you,_ sir. [_To himself._] Oh, if the Dean only knew the good thing I could put him on to for the Durnstone Handicap! [_He goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Children! Salome! Sheba! Here is good news!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Running to him._] Good news!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. What is it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Your Aunt!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Left us some money?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Your Aunt is coming to live with us.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. To what?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. To live with us! What Aunt?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My dear widowed sister, Georgiana Tidman.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. What's she like?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We don't want her.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Good gracious! Georgiana and I reconciled after all these years! She will help us to keep the expenses down.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Keep the expenses down!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Embracing his daughters._] A second mother to my girls. She will implant the precepts of retrenchment if their father cannot!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. But, Papa, who is Aunt what's-her-name?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Who is she?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My dears--a mournful, miserable history! [_With his head bent he walks to a chair, and holds out his hands to the girls, who go to him and kneel at his feet._] When you were infants your Aunt Georgiana married an individual whose existence I felt it my sad duty never to recognize.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. A bad man?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. He died ten years ago, and, therefore, we will say a misguided man. He was a person who bred horses to run in races for amusement combined with profit. He was also what is called a Gentleman Jockey, and it was your aunt's wifely boast that if ever he vexed her she could take a stone off his weight in half an hour. In due course his neck was dislocated.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. By Aunt?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Hush, child, no! You will be little wiser when I tell you he came a cropper!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. How awful it all sounds!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Left a widow, you would think it natural that Georgiana Tidman would have flown to her brother, himself a widower. Not at all. Maddened, I hope, by grief, she continued the career of her misguided husband, and for years, to use her own terrible words, she was "the Daisy of the Turf."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. What's that?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I don't know, toy-child. But at length retribution came. Ill luck fell upon her--her horses, stock, everything, came to the hammer. That was my hour. "Come to me," I wrote, "my children yearn for you."

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. [_With wry faces._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. "At the Deanery of St. Marvells, with the cares of a household, and a stable which contains only a thirteen-year-old pony, you may obtain rest and forgetfulness." And she is coming!

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. When? Oh! when?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. She merely says, "Soon."

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. [_Stamping with vexation._] Ugh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Salome, Sheba, you will, I fear, find her a sad broken creature, a weary fragment, a wave-tossed derelict. Let it be your patient endeavor to win back a flickering smile to the wan features of this chastened widow. _BLORE enters with a telegram._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. A telegram, sir! [_THE DEAN opens telegram._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. No Aunt Tidman flickers a smile at me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. I wouldn't be in her shoes for something!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Salt in her bed, Salome!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes, and the peg out of the rattling window! [_They grip hands earnestly._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Good gracious! Bless me! Girls, your Aunt Georgiana slept at the "Wheatsheaf," at Durnstone, last night, and is coming on this morning!

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. To-day!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Blore, tell Willis to get the chaise out. [_BLORE hurries out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Salome, child, you and I will drive into Durnstone--we may be in time to bring your Aunt over. My hat, Sheba! Quick! [_The clang of the gate bell is heard in the distance._] The bell! [_Looking out of window._] No--yes--it can't be! [_Speaking in an altered voice._] Children! I wonder if this is your Aunt Georgiana? [_BLORE appears with a half-frightened, surprised look._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Mrs. Tidman. _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters. She is a jovial, noisy woman, very "horsey" in manners and appearance, and dressed in pronounced masculine style, with billy cock hat and coaching coat. The girls cling to each other; THE DEAN recoils._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Well, Gus, my boy, how are you?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Shocked._] Georgiana!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Patting THE DEAN'S cheeks._] You're putting on too much flesh, Augustin; they should give you a ten-miler daily in a blanket.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_With dignity._] My dear sister!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Are these your two-year-olds? [_To SALOME._] Kiss your Aunt! [_She kisses SALOME with a good hearty smack._] [_To SHEBA._] Kiss your Aunt! [_She embraces SHEBA, then stands between the two girls and surveys them critically, touching them alternately with the end of her cane._] Lord bless you both! What names do you run under?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. I--I am Salome.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. I am Sheba.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Looking at SHEBA._] Why, little 'un, your stable companion could give you a stone and then get her nose in front!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Who has been impatiently fuming._] Georgiana, I fear these poor innocents don't follow your well-intentioned but inappropriate illustrations.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Oh, we'll soon wake 'em up. Well, Augustin, my boy, it's nearly twenty years since you and I munched our corn together.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Our estrangement has been painfully prolonged.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Since then we've both run many races, though we've never met in the same events. The world has ridden us both pretty hard at times, Gus, hasn't it? We've been punished and pulled and led down pretty often, but here we are [_tapping him sharply in the chest with her cane_] sound in the wind yet. You're doing well, Gus, and they say you're going up the hill neck-and-neck with your Bishop. I've dropped out of it--the mares don't last, Gus--and it's good and kind of you to give me a dry stable and a clean litter, and to keep me out of the shafts of a "Shrewsbury and Talbot."

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_In a whisper to SALOME._] Salome, I don't quite understand her--but I like Aunt.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. So do I. But she's not my idea of a weary fragment or a chastened widow.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My dear Georgiana, I rejoice that you meet me in this affectionate spirit, and when--pardon me--when you have a little caught the _tone_ of the Deanery----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Oh, I'll catch it; if I don't the Deanery will a little catch _my_ tone--the same thing. [_SHEBA laughs._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Reprovingly._] Toy-child!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Trust George Tidd for setting things quite square in a palace or a puddle.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. George Tidd! Who is George Tidd?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. I am George Tidd--that was my racing name. Ask after George Tidd at Newmarket--they'll tell you all about me. My colors were crimson and black diamonds. There you are. [_Producing her pocket-handkerchief, which is crimson and black._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Dear me! Very interesting! Georgiana, my dear. One moment, children. [_The girls go into the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Tapping the handkerchief._] I understand distinctly from your letter that all this is finally abandoned?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Worse luck! They'll never see my colors at the post again!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. And the contemplation of sport generally as a mental distraction----?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Oh, yes--I dare say you'll manage to wean me from that, too, in time.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. In time! Well, but--Georgiana! [_The gate bell is heard again, the girls re-enter._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. There's a visitor. I'll tootle upstairs and have a groom down. [_To SALOME and SHEBA._] Make the running, girls. At what time do we feed, Augustin?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. There is luncheon at one o'clock.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Right. The air here is so fresh I sha'n't be sorry to get my nose-bag on. [_She stalks out, accompanied by the girls._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My sister, Georgiana--my widowed sister, Georgiana. Dear me, I am quite disturbed. Surely, surely the serene atmosphere of the Deanery will work a change. It must! It must! If not, what a grave mistake I have made. Good gracious! No, no, I won't think of it! Still, it is a little unfortunate that poor Georgiana should arrive here on the very eve of these terrible races at St. Marvells. _BLORE enters with a card._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Who is it, Blore? [_Reading the card._] "Sir Tristram Mardon." Dear, dear! Certainly, Blore, certainly. [_BLORE goes out._] Mardon--why, Mardon and I haven't met since Oxford. [_BLORE re-enters, showing in SIR TRISTRAM MARDON, a well-preserved man of about fifty, with a ruddy face and jovial manner, the type of the thorough English sporting gentleman. BLORE goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Hullo, Jedd, how are you?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My dear Mardon--are we boys again?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Boisterously._] Of course we are! Boys again! [_He hits THE DEAN violently in the chest._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Breathing heavily--to himself._] I quite forgot how rough Mardon used to be. How it all comes back to me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Think I'm changed?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Only in appearance!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I'm still a bachelor--got terribly jilted by a woman years ago and have run in blinkers ever since. Can't be helped, can it? You're married, aren't you?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_With dignity._] I have been a widower for fifteen years.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Oh lor'! awfully sorry--can't be helped though, can it? [_Seizing THE DEAN'S hand and squeezing it._] Forgive me, old chap.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Withdrawing his hand with pain._] O-o-oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I've re-opened an old wound--damned stupid of me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Hush, Mardon! Please!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. All right. What do you think I'm down here for?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. For the benefit of your health, Mardon?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Ha! ha! Never had an ache in my life; sha'n't come and hear you preach next Sunday, Gus.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I do not preach next Sunday!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. You'd better not! No, I'm here for the races.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. The races! Hush, my dear Mardon, my girls----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Girls! May I trot 'em into the paddock to-morrow?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Thank you, no.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Think it over. You've seen the list of Starters for the Durnstone Handicap----?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. No, I haven't.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Not! Look here! Sir Tristram Mardon's Dandy Dick, nine stone two, Tom Gallawood up! What do you think of that?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I don't think of anything like that!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Digging THE DEAN in the ribs._] Look out for my colors--black and white, and a pink cap--first past the post to-morrow.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Really, my dear Mardon----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Good heavens! Jedd, they talk about Bonny Betsy.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I grieve to hear it. The tongue of scandal----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Taking THE DEAN'S arm and walking him about._] Do you imagine, sir, for one moment, that Bonny Betsy, with a boy on her back, can get down that bill with those legs of hers?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Another _horse_, I presume?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. No, a bay mare. George Tidd knew what she was about when she stuck to Dandy Dick to the very last.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Aghast._] George--Tidd?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Georgiana Tidman. Dandy came out of her stable after she smashed.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Bless me!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Poor old George! I wonder what's become of her.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. My dear Mardon, I am of course heartily pleased to revive in this way our old acquaintance. I wish it were in my power to offer you the hospitality of the Deanery--but----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Don't name it. My horse and I are over the way at "The Swan." Come and look at Dandy Dick!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Mardon, you don't understand. My position in St. Marvells----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Oh, I see, Jedd. I beg your pardon. You mean that the colors you ride in don't show up well on the hill yonder or in the stable of the "Swan" Inn.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. You must remember----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I remember that in your young days you made the heaviest book on the Derby of any of our fellows.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I always lost, Mardon; indeed, I always lost!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I remember that you once matched a mare of your own against another of Lord Beckslade's for fifty pounds!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Yes, but she wasn't in it, Mardon--I mean she was dreadfully beaten.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Shaking his head sorrowfully._] Oh Jedd, Jedd--other times, other manners. Good-bye, old boy.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. You're not--you're not offended, Mardon?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Taking THE DEAN'S hand._] Offended! No--only sorry, Dean, damned sorry, to see a promising lad come to an end like this. [_GEORGIANA enters with SALOME on one side of her and SHEBA on the other--all three laughing and chatting, apparently the best of friends._] By Jove! No! what--Tidd?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Hullo, Mardon! [_They shake hands warmly._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Of all places in the world, to find "Mr. Tidd!" [_Roaring with laughter._] Ho! ho! ho!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Laughing._] Ha! ha!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Why, Dean, you've been chaffing me, have you?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. No!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Yes, you have--you've been roasting your old friend!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_With dignity._] Mardon!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Tidd is a pal of yours, eh? Ho! ho!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Ha! ha!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Sir Tristram Mardon, Mrs. Tidman is my sister.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Your sister?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Yes, I've been running a bit dark, Mardon, but that stout, well-seasoned animal over there and this skittish creature come of the same stock and were foaled in the same stable. [_Pointing to SALOME and SHEBA._] There are a couple of yearlings here, you don't know. My nieces--Salome and Sheba.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Bowing._] How do you do? [_Heartily taking GEORGIANA'S hand again._] Well, I don't care whose sister you are, but I'm jolly glad to see you, George, my boy.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Gracious, Tris, don't squeeze my hand so!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_In horror._] Salome, Sheba, children! I must speak to you. Excuse me, Mardon. [_To himself._] Oh, what shall I do with my widowed sister? [_He goes into the garden._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_To SALOME._] That's like pa, just as we were getting interested.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. We'll come back in a minute. [_They go out by the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Lord! How odd! You know your brother and I were at Oxford together, George?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Were you, Tris! Then are you putting up here?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. He won't have me.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Won't have you!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Because I'm down here racing. You see, he's a Dean.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Is he? Well, then, you just lay a thousand sovereigns to a gooseberry that in this house I'm a Dean, too!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I suppose he's thinking of the Canons--and the Bishop--and those chaps.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Lord bless your heart, they're all right when you cheer them up a bit! If I'm here till the autumn meeting you'll find me lunching on the hill, with the Canons marking my card and the dear old Bishop mixing the salad. So say the word, Tris--I'll make it all right with Augustin.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. No, thanks, old fellow. The fact is I'm fixed at the "Swan" with--what do you think, George?--with Dandy Dick.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Oh! my old Dandy!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I brought him down with me in lavender. You know he runs for the Durnstone Handicap to-morrow.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Know! There's precious little that horse does that I don't know, and what I don't know I dream. Is he fit?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. As a fiddle--shines like a mirror--not an ounce too much or too little. He'll romp in!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. He'll dance in! Tris Mardon!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Eh?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Mysteriously._] Tris, Dandy Dick doesn't belong to you--not _all_ of him.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. No--I've only a half share. At your sale he was knocked down to John Fielder the trainer. The other half belongs to John.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. No, it doesn't, it belongs to _me!_

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. George!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Yes, directly I saw Dandy Dick marched out before the auctioneer I asked John Fielder to help me, and he did, like a Briton. For I can't live without horseflesh, if it's only a piece of cat's meat on a skewer. But when I condescended to keep company with the Canons and the Bishop here I promised Augustin that I wouldn't own anything on four legs, so John sold you half of Dick, and I can swear I don't own a horse--and I don't--not a whole one. But half a horse is better than no bread, Tris--and we're partners.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Roaring with laughter._] Ho! ho! ha! ha! ha!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What are you laughing at, man?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Oh, the Dean! the Dean! _SALOME and SHEBA enter unperceived._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Still laughing._] I--ho! ho!--I beg your pardon, George--ha! ha! Well, now you know he's fit, of course, you're going to back Dandy Dick for the Durnstone Handicap.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Back him! For every penny I've got in the world. That isn't much, but if I'm not a richer woman by a thousand pounds to-morrow night I shall have had a bad day.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh, Sheba! [_The girls come towards the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Discovering them._] Hush! [_To the girls._] Hallo!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. It's only us, Aunt. [_The girls go into the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I'll be off.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Keep your eye on the old horse, Tristram.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Don't fear. Good-morning, George!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Good-morning, partner! [_SIR TRISTRAM bursts out laughing again, she joining in the laughter._] Oh, do be quiet!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Ho! ho! ho! Ha! ha! Oh, say good-bye for me to the Dean! [_She gives him a push and he goes out._ _SHEBA and SALOME immediately re-enter from the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Aunt--dear Aunt----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Well, girls?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Aunt--Salome has something to say to you.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. No, it's Sheba.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Why, you're shivering all over. [_Catching hold of SHEBA._] Hallo, little 'un!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Aunt--dear Aunt Georgiana--we heard you say something about a thousand pounds.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. You've been listening?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. No--we only merely heard. And, oh, Aunt, a thousand pounds is such a lot, and we poor girls want such a little.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Money?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes. Salome has rather got into debt.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. My gracious!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. I haven't, any more than you have, Sheba.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Well, I'm in debt too, but I only meant to beg for Salome; but now I ask for both of us. Oh, Aunt Tidman, papa has told us that you have known troubles.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. So I have--heaps of them.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, I'm so glad. Because Salome and I are weary fragments too--we're everything awful but chastened widows. We owe forty pounds unknown to Pa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Forty pounds, nineteen.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Why, you ought to be ashamed of yourselves, you girls!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We are!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. We are!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. To cry and go on like this about forty pounds!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. But we've only got fifteen and threepence of our own in the world! And, oh, Aunt, you know something about the Races, don't you?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Eh?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. If you do, help two poor creatures to win forty pounds, nineteen. Aunt Georgiana, what's "Dandy Dick" you were talking to that gentleman about?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Child! Dandy Dick's a horse.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. We thought so. Then let Dandy Dick win _us_ some money.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. No, no! I won't hear of it!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, do, do!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh, do, do, do!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Go away--I won't. I say decidedly, I will not!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, do, do!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Do! Do, and we'll love you for ever and ever, Aunt Georgiana.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. You will! [_She embraces them heartily._] Bless your little innocent faces! Do you want to win forty pounds?

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. Yes, yes!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Do you want to win _fifty_ pounds?

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA and SALOME. Oh, yes, yes!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Taking her betting book from her pocket._] Very well, then, put your very petticoats on Dandy Dick! [_The girls stand clutching their skirts, frightened._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
text: END OF THE FIRST ACT.

title: Dandy Dick
text: THE SECOND ACT.

title: Dandy Dick
text: The morning-room at the Deanery, with the fire and the lamps lighted. It is after dinner. SHEBA is playing the piano, SALOME lolling upon the settee, and GEORGIANA pouring out tea. They are in evening dress.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Sugar, Sally? I call you Sally, Salome--the evening's too short for your name.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. All right, Aunt George--two lumps, please.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_To SHEBA._] Little 'un?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Two lumps and one in the saucer, to eat.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Quite a relief to shake off the gentlemen, isn't it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Do you think so, Aunt?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, _I_ don't think so.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. H'm! Now I understand why my foot was always in the way under the dinner-table. [_She holds out two cups, which the girls take from her._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. I thought the dinner was an overwhelming success.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. All our dinners are at the Deanery.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Awfully jolly. Mutton was overdone.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. That's our new cook's one failing.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. But the potatoes weren't--they rattled.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Cook never can manage potatoes.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What was wrong with the custards?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Well, it was Cook's first attempt at custards.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. However, they served one useful end. Now we _know_ the chimney wants sweeping.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. But it was a frightfully jolly dinner--take it all round.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes, take it all round. One has to take things all round.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What made us all so sad and silent--taking us all round?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Dear Papa was as lively as an owl with neuralgia.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Major Tarver isn't a conversational cracker.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Gerald Tarver has no liver--to speak of.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. He might have spoken about his lungs or something, to cheer us up.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. I fancy Mr. Darbey was about to make a witty remark once.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Yes, and then the servant handed him a dish and he shied at it. So we lost that.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Still, we ought to congratulate ourselves upon--upon a----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Upon a--upon a----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Upon a frightfully jolly dinner. [_Taking her betting book from her pocket._] Excuse me, girls. I've some figures to work out. If Dandy Dick hasn't fed better at the "Swan" than we have at the Deanery, he won't be in the first three. [_Reckoning._] Let me see.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_To SHEBA._] All's settled, Sheba, isn't it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_To SALOME._] Yes--everything. Directly the house is silent we let ourselves out at the front door.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. How do we get in again?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. By this window. It has a patent safety fastening, so it can be opened with a hairpin.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. We're courageous girls, aren't we?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Yes, I don't consider we're ordinary young ladies, at all.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. If we had known Aunt a little longer we might have confided in her and taken her with us.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Poor Aunt--we mustn't spoil her.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_Speaking outside._] I venture to differ with you, my dear Dean.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Here come the wax-works! [_She joins the girls as DARBEY enters through the Library, patronizing THE DEAN, who accompanies him._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Haw! I've just been putting the Dean right about a little army question, Mrs.--Mrs.---- I can't catch your name.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Don't try--you'd come out in spots, like measles. [DARBEY _stands by her, blankly, then attempts a conversation._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_To SALOME and SHEBA._] Children, it is useless to battle against it much longer.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Against what, Papa?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. A feeling of positive distaste for Mr. Darbey.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Oh, Papsey--think what Wellington was at his age. _MAJOR TARVER enters, pale and haggard._ _SALOME meets him._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Major!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_With a gasp._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Not well again?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Indigestion. I'm always like this after dinner.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. But what would you do if the trumpet summoned you to battle?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Oh, I suppose I should pack up a few charcoal biscuits and toddle out, you know.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_To DARBEY._] I've never studied the Army Guide.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. You're thinking of----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. The Turf Guide--beg pardon. I mean, the Army keeps a string of trained nurses, doesn't it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. There _are_ Army nurses.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Certainly. I was wondering whether your Colonel will send one with a perambulator to fetch you at about half-past eight. [_She leaves DARBEY and goes to THE DEAN. SHEBA joins DARBEY at the piano._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Well, Gus, my boy, you seem out of condition.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. I'm rather anxious for the post to bring to-day's "Times." You know I've offered a thousand pounds to our Restoration Fund.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Hush--I'll tell you. [_They talk in undertones. BLORE enters to remove the tea-tray._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Jumping up excitedly--to SALOME._] Eh? Oh, certainly--delighted! [_Singing to himself._] "Come into the garden, Maud, for the black bat----"

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Now you're yourself again.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. I'm always dreadfully excited when I'm asked to sing. It's as good as a carbonate of soda lozenge to me to be asked to sing. [_To BLORE._] My music is in my overcoat pocket. [_BLORE crosses to the door._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. And Mr. Darbey has brought his violin.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_In a rage, glaring at DARBEY._] Hah! There now!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To BLORE._] You'll find it in the hall. [_BLORE goes out. THE DEAN dozes in a chair. SALOME and SHEBA talk to GEORGIANA at the table._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To himself._] He always presumes with his confounded fiddle when I'm going to entertain. He knows that his fiddle's never hoarse and that I am, sometimes.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To himself._] Tarver always tries to cut me out with his elderly Chest C. He ought to put it on the Retired List.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. I'll sing him off his legs to-night--I'm in lovely voice. [_He walks into the Library and is heard trying his voice, singing "Come into the garden, Maud."_

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_To himself._] He needn't bother himself. While he was dozing in the carriage I threw his music out of the window. _TARVER re-enters triumphantly._ _BLORE re-enters, carrying a violin-case and a leather music roll. DARBEY takes the violin-case, opens it, and produces his violin and music. BLORE hands the music roll to TARVER and goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To SALOME, trembling with excitement._] My tones are like a beautiful bell this evening. I'm so glad, for all our sakes. [_As he takes the leather music roll from BLORE._] Thank you, that's it.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. What will you begin with?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. "Come into the garden, Maud." I've begun with "Corne into the garden, Maud" for years and years. [_He opens the music roll--it is empty._] Oh! Miss Jedd, I've forgotten my music!

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. Oh! Major Tarver! [_TARVER with a groan of despair sinks on to the settee._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Never mind--Mr. Darbey will play.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_Tuning his violin._] Will you accompany me?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Raising her eyes._] To the end of the world. [_She sits at the piano._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. My mother says that my bowing is something like Joachim's, and she ought to know.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. Why?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Oh, because she's heard Joachim. [_DARBEY plays and SHEBA accompanies him. SALOME sits beside TARVER._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_To herself._] Well, after all, George, my boy, you're not stabled in such a bad box! Here is a regular pure, simple, English Evening at Home!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Mumbling to himself._] A thousand pounds to the Restoration Fund and all those bills to settle--oh dear! oh dear! What shall I do?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_To herself._] I hope my ball-dress will drive all the other women mad!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_To himself--glaring at DARBEY._] I feel I should like to garrote him with his bass string.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Frowning at her betting book._] I think I shall hedge a bit over the Crumbleigh Stakes.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_As he plays, glancing at TARVER._] I wonder how old Tarver's Chest C likes a holiday.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_As she plays._] We must get Pa to bed early. Dear Papa's always so dreadfully in the way.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Looking around._] No--there's nothing like it in any other country. A regular, pure, simple, English Evening at Home! _BLORE enters quickly, cutting "The Times" with a paper-knife as he enters._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. The paper's just arrived. [_The music stops abruptly--all the ladies glare at BLORE and hush him down._

title: Dandy Dick
text: GEORGIANA, SALOME, _and_ SHEBA. Sssssh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Taking the paper from BLORE._] This is my fault--there may be something in "The Times" of special interest to me. Thank you, Blore. [_BLORE goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. Ha, ha, ha! spoilt his pianissimo!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Scanning the paper._] Oh, I can't believe it!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What's the matter?

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
text: TARVER _and_ DARBEY. The Dean!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Children! Georgiana! Friends! My munificent offer has produced the desired result.

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Seven wealthy people, including three brewers, have come forward with a thousand pounds apiece in aid of the restoration of the Minster Spire!

title: Dandy Dick
text: SALOME _and_ SHEBA. [_Horrified._] Ah!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. That means a cool thousand out of your pocket, Gus.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Yes. [_Reading._] "The anxiety to which The Dean of St. Marvells has so long been a victim will now doubtless be relieved." [_With his hand to his head._] I suppose I shall feel the relief to-morrow.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. What's wrong with the Spire? Nobody sleeps in it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. It _is_ a little out of repair--but hardly sufficiently so to warrant the presumptuous interference of three brewers. Excuse me, I think I'll enjoy the fresh air for a moment. [_He goes to the window and draws back the curtains--a bright red glare is seen in the sky._] Bless me! Look there!

title: Dandy Dick
text: GEORGIANA, SALOME, _and_ SHEBA. Oh! what's that?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. It's a conflagration!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. [_Clinging to TARVER._] Where is it? Are we safe?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_Clinging to DARBEY._] Where is it? Are we safe?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Where is it? _BLORE enters with a scared look._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_To BLORE._] Where is it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: ALL
text: ALL. Where is it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. The old Swan Inn's a-fire! [_The gate-bell is heard ringing violently in the distance. BLORE goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Uttering a loud screech._] The Swan Inn! [_Madly._] You girls, get me a hat and coat. Somebody fetch me a pair of boots! [_SALOME, SHEBA, and TARVER go to the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Georgiana!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Don't talk to me! [_To TARVER._] Lend me your boots!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. I daren't. If I once get cold extremities----

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Ah! [_She is going, THE DEAN stops her._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Respect yourself, Georgiana--where are you going?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Going! I'm going to help clear the stables at The Swan!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Remember what you are--my sister--a lady!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. I'm not. George Tidd's a man, every inch of her! [_SIR TRISTRAM rushes in breathlessly. GEORGIANA rushes at him and clutches his coat._] Tris Mardon, speak!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Exhausted._] Oh!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. The horse? The horse! You've got him out?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Yes, safe and sound.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Safe and sound! That old horse has backed himself to win the handicap. [_She sinks into a chair. TARVER and DARBEY with SALOME and SHEBA stand looking out of the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. George, his tail is singed a bit.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. The less weight for him to carry to-morrow. [_Beginning to cry._] Dear old Dandy, he never was much to look at.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. The worst of it is, the fools threw two pails of cold water over him to put it out.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Oh! that's done him!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Now, my dear Georgiana! what is a horse?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. A living example to a Dean. [_THE DEAN goes distractedly into the Library._] Where is the animal?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. My man Hatcham is running him up and down the lane here to try to get him warm again.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Where are you going to put the homeless beast up now?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. I don't know.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Starting up._] I do though!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Madwoman! What are you going to do?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Bring Dandy Dick into our stables!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. No, no!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. The very place!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Georgiana, pray consider _me!_

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. So I will, when you've had two pails of water thrown over you. [_THE DEAN walks about in despair._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Mardon, I appeal to _you!_

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Oh, Dean, Dean, I'm ashamed of you!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_To SIR TRISTRAM._] Are you ready?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. [_Takes off his coat and throws it over GEORGIANA'S shoulders._] George, you're a brick!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. A brick, am I? [_Quietly to him._] One partner pulls Dandy out of the Swan--t'other one leads Dandy into the Deanery. Quits, my lad! [_They go out together._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. What is happening to me! It will be in all the sporting papers. "Sir Tristram Mardon's Dandy Dick reflected great credit upon the Deanery Stables!" "The Sporting Dean!" [_He walks into the Library, where he sinks into a chair, as SALOME, TARVER, DARBEY and SHEBA come from the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. They're getting the flames under. If I had had my goloshes with me I should have been here, there, and everywhere.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Where there's a crowd of Civilians the Military exercise a wise discretion in restraining themselves.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SHEBA
text: SHEBA. [_To TARVER and DARBEY._] You had better go now; then we'll get the house quiet as soon as possible. Poor Papa looks worried.

title: Dandy Dick
text: SHEBA _and_ SALOME. Poor Papa!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. We will wait with the carriage in the lane.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Yes, yes. [_Calling._] Papa, Major Tarver and Mr. Darbey must go. [_She rings the bell. THE DEAN comes from the Library._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. Dear me, I'm very remiss!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: TARVER
text: TARVER. [_Shaking hands._] Most fascinating evening!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_Shaking hands._] Charming, my dear Dean. _BLORE enters._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Major Tarver's carriage.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: BLORE
text: BLORE. Hat the gate, Miss Salome.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SALOME
text: SALOME. Don't risk the cold, Papa. [_BLORE goes out, followed by SHEBA, SALOME, and TARVER. DARBEY is going, when he returns to THE DEAN._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. By-the-bye, my dear Dean--come over and see me. We ought to know more of each other. Say Monday.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Restraining his anger._] I will _not_ say Monday!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. Any time you like. Oh--and I say--let me know when you preach, and I'll get some of our fellows to give their patronage! [_He goes out._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Closing the door after him with a bang._] Another moment--another moment--and I fear I should have been violently rude to him, a guest under my roof! [_He walks up to the fireplace and stands looking into the fire, as DARBEY. having forgotten his violin, returns to the room._] Oh, Blore, now understand me, if that Mr. Darbey ever again presumes to present himself at the Deanery I will not see him!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: DARBEY
text: DARBEY. [_With his violin in his hand, haughtily._] I've come back for my violin. [_Goes out with dignity._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: THE DEAN
text: THE DEAN. [_Horrified._] Oh, Mr. Darbey! Hear an explanation, Mr. Darbey! [_He runs out after DARBEY. GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Don't be down, Tris, my boy; cheer up, lad, he'll be fit yet, bar a chill! Aha! he knew me, he knew me when I kissed his dear old nose!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. He'd be a fool of a horse if he hadn't felt deuced flattered at that.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. He's no fool. He knows he's in the Deanery too. Did you see him cast up his eyes and lay his ears back when I led him in?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. Oh, George, George, it's such a pity about his tail!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. [_Cheerily._] Not it. You watch his head to-morrow--that'll come in first. [_HATCHAM, a groom, looks in at the window._

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: HATCHAM
text: HATCHAM. Are you there, Sir?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. What is it?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: HATCHAM
text: HATCHAM. I jest run round to tell you that Dandy is a feedin' as steady as a baby with a bottle.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Don't you close your eyes all night.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: HATCHAM
text: HATCHAM. Not me, mum. And I've got hold of the constable 'ere, Mr. Topping--he's going to sit up with me, for company's sake.

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: SIR TRISTRAM
text: SIR TRISTRAM. The constable?

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: HATCHAM
text: HATCHAM. Yes, Sir Tristram. [_Coming forward mysteriously._] Why, bless you and the lady, sir--supposin' the fire at the "Swan" warn't no accident!

title: Dandy Dick
speaker: GEORGIANA
text: GEORGIANA. Eh?
